_strings.@@40c689856e8a: Treaty conformity — NC conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from NC income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the NC return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: NC conforms. The 2025 D-401 instructions state for Form D-400 Schedule S: "The starting point for North Carolina taxable income is federal adjusted gross income as of January 1, 2023" (the 2025 booklet keeps the January 1, 2023 conformity date and adds expressly that OBBBA changes do not apply for tax year 2025 unless NC conforms). Because federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI, it flows through to NC untaxed UNLESS NC adds it back. The 2025 Form D-400 Schedule S, Part A "Additions to Federal Adjusted Gross Income" list, as enumerated line-by-line in the 2025 D-401 (Line 1 interest from obligations of states other than NC; Line 2 deferred gains reinvested into a qualified Opportunity Fund under IRC 1400Z-2; Line 3 85% of bonus depreciation — NC did not adopt IRC 168(k) or the new IRC 168(n); Line 4 85% of the IRC 179 difference; Line 5 S-corporation shareholder built-in gains tax; Line 6 amount by which federal basis exceeds state basis on property disposed of in 2025; Line 7 federal net operating loss deduction; Line 8 state/local/foreign income tax deducted under IRC 164 by an S corporation, partnership, or estate and trust; Line 9 withdrawal of 529 plan contributions not used for qualified purposes; Line 10 discharge of qualified principal residence indebtedness; Line 11 qualified education loan payments paid by an employer excluded under IRC 127(c); Line 12 expenses allocable to income exempt or excluded; Line 13 discharge of certain student loan debt; Line 14 taxed pass-through entity loss; Line 15 "Reserved for Future Use. Do not enter an amount on this line."; Line 16 "Total Additions. Add Lines 1 through 15") contains NO add-back of treaty-exempt income. Since treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed, conforms_to_federal_treaties = true. Note one nuance to flag for filers: Schedule S Part A Line 12 requires adding back EXPENSES allocable to income exempt from NC tax, but it does not add back the exempt income itself. (For 2025 the whole Part A list is transcribed — the 2024 pack's unverified gap on Lines 14-15 is CLOSED: Line 14 is the taxed pass-through entity loss and Line 15 is expressly reserved and left blank.)

If zero or less, enter a zero." Line 6 starts from federal AGI; Line 12b = Line 8 (federal AGI + Schedule S Part A additions) minus Line 12a (Line 9 deductions + Line 10b child deduction + Line 11 N.C. standard/itemized deduction). This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Rate change: the individual income tax rate dropped to 4.25% (0.0425) for tax year 2025 (from 4.5% in 2024 and 4.75% in 2023) — 2025 D-401 "What is the Tax Rate?", re-verified on the 2025 Form D-400 Line 15. The NC Standard Deduction Chart is UNCHANGED from 2024/2023. NC does NOT conform to the 2025 federal reconciliation act ("OBBBA"): the 2025 D-401 states NC's starting point is federal AGI as of January 1, 2023, and that NC "does not conform to the federal standard deduction amount, to the federal itemized deduction amount, or to the federal additional deductions reported on federal Schedule 1-A" — never substitute a federal 2025 standard deduction for the NC chart amount. Standard-deduction gates NOT modeled by calc.state_tax: MFS gets $0 if the spouse claims itemized deductions, and the N.C. standard deduction is ZERO for anyone not eligible for the FEDERAL standard deduction (see federal Pub 501; the filing chart lists nonresident aliens at $0) — itemizers use D-400 Line 11 itemized deductions (Form D-400 Schedule A) instead; compute those cases on the form. There is no additional NC standard deduction for age 65 or older or blind. N.C. child deduction (D-400 Line 10) is NOT modeled: up to $3,000 per qualifying child (a child for whom the federal child tax credit was allowed for 2025), stepping down $3,000/$2,500/$2,000/$1,500/$1,000/$500/$0 by federal AGI (MFJ/Qualifying Widow(er)/Surviving Spouse brackets up to $40,000 ... over $140,000; HoH up to $30,000 ... over $105,000; Single/MFS up to $20,000 ... over $70,000) — the 2025 D-401 Child Deduction Table is unchanged from 2024; take it from the Child Deduction Worksheet, not from a per-dependent exemption. North Carolina has no personal or dependent exemptions.
